passage:
Engineers built a small model of an ancient bridge to test how it stood without modern materials. Students watched as weight was added.
The arch shape spread pressure to the sides. The bridge held more than students expected.
The engineer explained that ancient builders learned from observation, failure, and experience. They did not have modern computers, but they had deep practical knowledge.
Students stopped thinking of old technology as simple.
The model showed that intelligence can be built into shape. A bridge is not only stone. It is mathematics, labor, and memory arranged so people can cross.
